role: The ONE art-side statement of the museum twin family: which files in patent-portfolio/ have a twin in ~/projects/awkronos/patents, what the relationship between the copies is, and the measured pins that hold that statement. Prose elsewhere (DEBT-museum-navigation-duplication.md, module headers, commit messages) points here and does not restate numbers.

law.one_ssot: Numbers live in this file and are produced by tests/unit/twin-measure.mjs from two trees. A second copy of a pin is a fork, and this family has already been caught with one that rotted.
law.union_not_revert: Divergent content is recorded with a digest, never silently deleted, and never reverted to whichever copy scored better. A pair whose two sides each hold unique lines is declared diverged and left alone.
law.similarity_never_authorizes_consolidatio: SimHash/hamming scores classify; they do not prove identity and they do not license a merge or a deletion. Only sha256 over the declared recipe pins bytes. A code_map_rsi_targets rankScore is band order, not a measured quantity.
law.byte_identity_is_recipe_scoped: 'Identical' always names the recipe it was measured under — doc-header, comment-header or whole — because every pair in this family that looks identical as a body is different as a whole file, by header design.
law.guards_are_measured_not_authored: A guards row names an INSTRUMENT and carries the state of that instrument as measured on this host (PRESENT / ABSENT / UNMEASURED, by guardLegs()). The sentence alone is not evidence that a gate exists: patents' 6-leg census guard and the pre-commit it was wired to had been deleted from the surviving lineage while the row still announced them, which is why R13 re-runs the same ls-tree on every run and why an ABSENT word here is a fact about a published surface, not a defect to be re-worded away.

basis.art_pin_channel: blob + sha256 of the tree bytes, per pair row. No art commit sha is recorded: the register is committed INTO the commit its own HEAD value would name, so that value could only ever be stale — and the art side does not need it, because R2 re-measures these bytes against the checkout on every run. Cite the ref in a commit message or the lane envelope, never here.

geometry_agreement.why: navigation.js reads DIMENSIONS from ./architecture.js. These are its keys, measured in both copies of architecture.js, so 'port navigation whole' is a checked claim and not a re-argument of DEBT residual text.
geometry_agreement.note: read_by_navigation is the set the tripwire re-derives from navigation.js's own source on every run; debt_port_checklist is what the DEBT note asks a port lane to verify; diverged_unread is recorded with both values because it is a real divergence the pair's own file cannot be broken by — declared, not consolidated, and not this lane's to merge.

published.nature: No digest is recorded in this leg, deliberately. refs/remotes/origin/main is THIS repo's own moving tip, and the register is committed into the very commits that move it, so there is no commit this file could name that would make a recorded value true (basis.art_pin_channel states that law; this leg used to break it). What breaking it cost: the row recorded the blob the tip carried at generation, so it went false the moment the fold that changed these bytes landed, `node scripts/twin-register.mjs --check` could no longer be satisfied on trunk, and the register was naming a digest none of its own tests could recompute — residual 1's defect one field over, wearing a smaller hat. The live question ('do these bytes match what the tip carries now?') is measured, not recorded: R3 re-reads the ref on every run and, when the two differ, proves with merge-base --is-ancestor whether this checkout is ahead of that tip at all.

patents_leg.what: museum/navigation.js at 58ef6462 'wip: banked before fleet git-sync' (2026-08-29) — the head the generation recorded as patents refs/remotes/origin/main. Whether that commit sits on live main's history is measured below (merge_base_is_ancestor_rc: 0 — it IS an ancestor, so the generation's ref was honest about lineage and only about content wrong); either way the published tip carries a different navigation.js blob than the one this leg names, and THAT is the finding — a census row scored on bytes no published surface holds

census_provenance.reading: Both 're_measured_here.blob' rows reproduce the hex the generation pinned, so the generation is not wrong about the bytes it read — it read a parked checkout on one side and a banked wip commit on the other. Patents' published row is a different hex from its generation leg and is re-readable at basis.patents_tip; art's published row records no hex at all, because the ref it would quote is this repo's own tip (see that leg's nature). Either way the census was scored on non-published trees, and the live comparison is R3's job on every run rather than a value stored here.

The census reads whatever tree a host happens to have checked out, which is why a pair closed in 2026-10-26 keeps re-serving as live copy debt. This host's shared art checkout and its patents counterpart are therefore NOT necessarily at their published tips — and no position is recorded in this file, because a committed working-tree count goes false on the next fetch or push and would be the same rot wearing a smaller hat. tests/unit/museum-twin-register.test.mjs R11 measures it on every run instead, with `git -C <repo> rev-list --count HEAD..refs/remotes/origin/main` in both repos, and prints the two counts as a diagnostic. Fast-forwarding a checkout belongs to whoever owns it, not to a lane. The same law caught one more value at the landing of residual 1: this row's own art_leg.published used to store the blob refs/remotes/origin/main carried for navigation.js at generation, which went false the instant the fold landed (measured: `--check` rc=1 on trunk with exactly one differing leaf, that one) — a register cannot name the commit that would make it true, because it is committed into those commits. It stores no digest now and R3 measures the ref live; patents_leg.published keeps its hex because patents is not this repo and basis.patents_tip names the commit to re-read it at, which R10 and R11 assert.
